chunks: 6. He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, who reported from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abu 'Umayr, from more than one of his companions, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali,

who said: One who was present when Abdul Malik ibn Marwan was addressing the people in Makkah reported to me. When he reached the part of admonition in his sermon, a man stood up and said: "Wait, wait! You command but do not follow, you forbid but do not refrain, you admonish but take no heed. Should we follow your example? Or obey your orders? If you say: 'Follow our example', how can we follow the example of the oppressors? And what is the justification for following the culprits who usurped the wealth of God for their state and turned the servants of God into their slaves?

And if you say: 'Obey our orders and accept our advice', how can one advise others when one deceives oneself? And how can obedience to the unjust be obligatory? And if you say: 'Take the words of wisdom wherever you find them, and accept the admonitions from whoever you hear them', then perhaps there are among us those more eloquent in the types of admonitions, and more acquainted with the uses of language than you are. So remove yourselves from it, open up its locks and leave the way open, so that those whom you have scattered in the country, and transferred from their abode to every valley, may take charge.

By God, we did not give you the reins of our affairs, nor give you authority over ourselves, our wealth and our faith so that you may act in the manner of despots; except that we endure ourselves for the fulfilment of the appointed time, the attainment of the end, and the completion of the trial. For every one of you there is a day he cannot escape, and a book of record he must read; a record that does not leave anything small or big without counting it.
'And those who do wrong shall soon come to know what punishment awaits them' [26:227].
He said: Then some armed men arrested him. That was the last time we saw him, and we do not know what was meted out to him.

key_terms.الجبارين: Despots, tyrants who rule through force and coercion
key_terms.العظة: Admonition, sermon meant to instill moral awareness
key_terms.المحنة: Trial, tribulation — refers to the ordained period of suffering under unjust rule
key_terms.سيرة: Conduct, way of life, example set by one's actions

ai.seo_question: What did the man say to Abdul Malik ibn Marwan during his sermon in Makkah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Mufid describes a courageous confrontation during the Umayyad period. An unnamed man publicly challenged the Umayyad caliph Abdul Malik ibn Marwan during his sermon at Makkah, exposing the hypocrisy of rulers who preach virtue while practicing tyranny. The man systematically dismantled every possible justification for the Umayyad claim to authority, concluding with a Quranic warning about divine retribution. He was arrested by the caliph's guards and was never seen again, illustrating the persecution of dissent under Umayyad rule.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 6. He said: Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, who reported from ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa’dabadi, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abu Umair, from more than one of his companions, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali,

who reported from one who was present when Abdul Malik ibn Marwan rose to address the people in Makkah. When he began the part of admonition during his sermon, a man stood up and said: "Wait, wait! You are from those who preach, but do not follow, you forbid but do not refrain from what you forbid. You admonish but take no lesson from your admonition. Can your example be emulated? Can your orders be obeyed? If you ask us to follow your example, how can we follow the example of the oppressors? And what is the justification for following the culprits who have usurped the wealth of Allah for their state, and have turned the slaves of Allah as their own slaves?

And if you say: ’Obey our orders and accept our advice’, how can one advise others when one deceives oneself, and how can obedience to the unjust be obligatory?’ And if you say: ’Take the (words of) wisdom wherever you find them, and accept the admonitions from whoever you hear them’, then perhaps there are among us more eloquent in the types of admonitions, and more acquainted with the uses of language than you are. So, remove yourselves from it, open up its locks and leave the way open, so that those whom you have scattered in the country, and transferred them from their abode to several places, may take the charge.

By Allah, we did not give you the reins of our affairs, and did not give you authority over ourselves, our wealth and our faith so that you may act in the manner of despots; except that we force ourselves to endure till the time comes, and the end is achieved, and the suffering is over. For everyone of you there is a day he cannot escape and a book of record he must read; a record that does not leave anything small or big without counting it.
’And those who do wrong shall soon come to know what punishment awaits them.’ [26:227]."
He said: Then some armed men arrested him. That was the last time we saw him, and we do not know what was meted out to him!
